# Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points

The uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points asks whether, for a number field $K$ and an
integer $g \geq 2$, there is a number $N(K, g)$ depending only on $K$ and $g$ such that every
algebraic curve of genus $g$ defined over $K$ has at most $N(K, g)$ $K$-rational points. Here an
algebraic curve over $K$ is a smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible variety of dimension
$1$ over $K$. Faltings' theorem says that each such curve has finitely many $K$-rational points;
the conjecture asks for a bound that is uniform in the curve.

Mathlib does not define the genus of a curve. This file defines it through the function field of
the curve: places of the function field $F/K$ are the normalized discrete valuations of $F$ that
are trivial on $K$, and the genus is $\max\{\deg D - \ell(D) + 1\}$ over all divisors $D$, where
$\ell(D)$ is the $K$-dimension of the Riemann–Roch space of $D$. This is Definition 1.4.15 in
[Sti2009]. For a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve $C$ over $K$ this is the usual
genus of $C$, and $C(K)$ is the set of sections of the structure morphism
$C \to \operatorname{Spec} K$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_rational_points)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [CHM1997] L. Caporaso, J. Harris, B. Mazur, *Uniformity of rational points*,
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1997), 1–35.
- [DGH2021] V. Dimitrov, Z. Gao, P. Habegger, *Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves*,
  Ann. of Math. 194 (2021), 237–298. [arXiv:2001.10276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10276)
- [Sti2009] H. Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, 2nd ed., Springer GTM 254.

universe u

section FunctionField

variable (K F : Type*) [Field K] [Field F] [Algebra K F]

/-- A place of the field extension `F / K`, given by its normalized valuation: a valuation
`v : F → ℤᵐ⁰` that is surjective (so `v` is a nontrivial discrete valuation with value group
`ℤ`) and trivial on `K`. For a function field `F` of one variable over `K` these are exactly the
places of `F / K` in the sense of [Sti2009], Definition 1.1.8, each equipped with its unique
normalized valuation. -/
structure Place where
  /-- The normalized valuation of the place. -/
  valuation : Valuation F ℤᵐ⁰
  /-- The valuation is normalized: its value group is all of `ℤ`. -/
  surjective : Function.Surjective valuation
  /-- The valuation is trivial on the constants `K`. -/
  valuation_algebraMap_eq_one : ∀ c : K, c ≠ 0 → valuation (algebraMap K F c) = 1

variable {K F}

namespace Place

theorem valuation_algebraMap_le_one (P : Place K F) (c : K) :
    P.valuation (algebraMap K F c) ≤ 1 := by
  by_cases hc : c = 0
  · simp [hc]
  · exact (P.valuation_algebraMap_eq_one c hc).le

theorem algebraMap_mem_valuationSubring (P : Place K F) (c : K) :
    algebraMap K F c ∈ P.valuation.valuationSubring :=
  P.valuation_algebraMap_le_one c

/-- The valuation ring of a place of `F / K` is a `K`-algebra. -/
noncomputable instance (P : Place K F) : Algebra K P.valuation.valuationSubring :=
  ((algebraMap K F).codRestrict P.valuation.valuationSubring
    P.algebraMap_mem_valuationSubring).toAlgebra

/-- The degree of a place `P` of `F / K`: the degree over `K` of the residue field of `P`.
The `K`-rational places are those of degree `1`. -/
noncomputable def deg (P : Place K F) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField P.valuation.valuationSubring)

end Place

variable (K F) in
/-- A divisor of `F / K`: a formal `ℤ`-linear combination of finitely many places. -/
abbrev Divisor := Place K F →₀ ℤ

/-- The degree of a divisor `D = ∑ n_P P` of `F / K` is `∑ n_P deg P`. -/
noncomputable def Divisor.deg (D : Divisor K F) : ℤ :=
  D.sum fun P n => n * P.deg

variable (K F) in
/-- The Riemann–Roch space of a divisor `D` of `F / K`: the `K`-subspace of `F` of elements `x`
with `v_P(x) ≥ -D(P)` at every place `P`. In multiplicative notation (where the valuation ring is
`{x | v_P x ≤ 1}`) this reads `v_P x ≤ exp (D P)`. -/
def riemannRochSpace (D : Divisor K F) : Submodule K F where
  carrier := {x | ∀ P : Place K F, P.valuation x ≤ WithZero.exp (D P)}
  zero_mem' P := by simp
  add_mem' {x y} hx hy P := (P.valuation.map_add x y).trans (max_le (hx P) (hy P))
  smul_mem' c x hx P := by
    rw [Algebra.smul_def, P.valuation.map_mul]
    calc P.valuation (algebraMap K F c) * P.valuation x ≤ 1 * P.valuation x :=
          mul_le_mul_left (P.valuation_algebraMap_le_one c) _
      _ = P.valuation x := one_mul _
      _ ≤ _ := hx P

/-- The constants `K` lie in the Riemann–Roch space of the zero divisor. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem algebraMap_mem_riemannRochSpace_zero (c : K) :
    algebraMap K F c ∈ riemannRochSpace K F 0 := fun P => by
  simpa using P.valuation_algebraMap_le_one c

variable (K F) in
/-- The dimension `ℓ(D)` over `K` of the Riemann–Roch space of a divisor `D` of `F / K`. -/
noncomputable def riemannRochDim (D : Divisor K F) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K (riemannRochSpace K F D)

variable (K F) in
/-- The genus of `F / K`, following [Sti2009], Definition 1.4.15:
$g = \max \{\deg D - \ell(D) + 1 : D \text{ a divisor of } F / K\}$.
For a function field `F` of one variable over `K` with `K` as its full field of constants, this
maximum exists by Riemann's theorem; it equals the genus of the smooth projective curve with
function field `F`. -/
noncomputable def genus : ℕ :=
  sSup {g : ℕ | ∃ D : Divisor K F, (g : ℤ) = D.deg - riemannRochDim K F D + 1}

/-- The rational function field `K(t)`, the function field of the projective line, has genus `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem genus_ratFunc : genus K (RatFunc K) = 0 := by
  sorry

end FunctionField

/-- The `K`-algebra structure on the function field of an integral scheme `C` over `K`, induced by
the structure morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`. -/
noncomputable def functionFieldAlgebra [IsIntegral C] : Algebra K C.functionField :=

    C.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint C) trivial).hom.toAlgebra

/-- The genus of an integral scheme `C` over `K`: the genus of its function field over `K`.

noncomputable def curveGenus [IsIntegral C] : ℕ :=

  genus K C.functionField

morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`. -/
def rationalPoints : Set (Spec (.of K) ⟶ C) :=

end Curve

$N(K, g)$ of $K$-rational points? That is: for every number field $K$ and every integer $g \geq 2$,
is there a number $N(K, g)$, depending only on $K$ and $g$, such that every smooth projective
geometrically irreducible curve $C$ of genus $g$ defined over $K$ satisfies $\# C(K) \leq N(K, g)$?

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points

The conjecture asserts that for every number field $K$ and every integer $g \geq 2$ there is a
number $N(K, g)$, depending only on $K$ and $g$, such that every (smooth, projective,
geometrically irreducible) algebraic curve $C$ of genus $g$ defined over $K$ has at most
$N(K, g)$ $K$-rational points.

Mathlib has no notion of the genus of a curve, so we use the classical dictionary between
curves and function fields (see e.g. Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, Ch. I §6 and Ch. IV, or
Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Ch. 1 and Ch. 4). Over a number field $K$
(so in characteristic $0$):

* smooth projective geometrically irreducible curves $C / K$ correspond, up to isomorphism, to
  algebraic function fields $F / K$ of one variable whose full constant field is $K$
  (i.e. $F$ is a finite extension of $K(x)$ for some $x$ transcendental over $K$, and $K$ is
  algebraically closed in $F$), via $F = K(C)$;
* the closed points of $C$ correspond to the places of $F / K$, i.e. the valuation subrings
  $\mathcal{O}_P \subsetneq F$ containing $K$; the $K$-rational points $C(K)$ correspond to the
  places of degree one, i.e. those with residue field $\mathcal{O}_P / \mathfrak{m}_P = K$;
* the genus of $C$ is $\dim_K H^0(C, \Omega^1_{C/K})$, the dimension of the space of global
  regular differentials, i.e. of the Kähler differentials $\omega \in \Omega_{F/K}$ with
  $v_P(\omega) \geq 0$ at every place $P$, where $v_P(f \, dt) = v_P(f)$ for a uniformizer $t$
  at $P$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_rational_points)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- L. Caporaso, J. Harris, B. Mazur, *Uniformity of rational points*,
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1997), 1–35.
- V. Dimitrov, Z. Gao, P. Habegger, *Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves*,
  Ann. of Math. 194 (2021), 237–298, [arXiv:2001.10276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10276)
-/

open IntermediateField

universe u v

variable (K F : Type*) [Field K] [Field F] [Algebra K F]

/-- `F` is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over `K`:
it is an algebraic function field of one variable over `K` (a finite extension of `K(x)` for some
`x` transcendental over `K`) whose full field of constants is `K` (every element of `F` algebraic
over `K` already lies in `K`). -/
structure IsCurveFunctionField : Prop where
  exists_transcendental : ∃ x : F, Transcendental K x ∧ Module.Finite K⟮x⟯ F
  mem_range_of_isAlgebraic : ∀ y : F, IsAlgebraic K y → y ∈ (algebraMap K F).range

/-- A place of `F / K`: a valuation subring `P` of `F` containing (the image of) `K` and
different from `F`. For a function field of one variable these are exactly the (discrete)
valuation rings of the closed points of the corresponding smooth projective curve. -/
def IsPlace (P : ValuationSubring F) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : K, algebraMap K F k ∈ P) ∧ P ≠ ⊤

/-- A place `P` of `F / K` is rational (has degree one) if its residue field is `K`, i.e. every
element of `P` is congruent modulo the maximal ideal of `P` to a constant. These places
correspond to the `K`-rational points of the curve. -/
def IsRationalPlace (P : ValuationSubring F) : Prop :=
  IsPlace K F P ∧
    ∀ x : F, P.valuation x ≤ 1 → ∃ k : K, P.valuation (x - algebraMap K F k) < 1

variable {F} in
/-- `t` is a uniformizer at the valuation subring `P`: it generates the maximal ideal of `P`. -/
def IsUniformizer (P : ValuationSubring F) (t : F) : Prop :=
  P.valuation t < 1 ∧ ∀ y : F, P.valuation y < 1 → P.valuation y ≤ P.valuation t

variable {K F} in
/-- Nonzero constants are units at every place of `F / K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 11 14]
theorem IsPlace.valuation_algebraMap {P : ValuationSubring F} (hP : IsPlace K F P) {k : K}
    (hk : k ≠ 0) : P.valuation (algebraMap K F k) = 1 := by
  have h1 : P.valuation (algebraMap K F k) ≤ 1 := (P.valuation_le_one_iff _).mpr (hP.1 k)
  have h2 : P.valuation (algebraMap K F k⁻¹) ≤ 1 := (P.valuation_le_one_iff _).mpr (hP.1 k⁻¹)
  have h3 : P.valuation (algebraMap K F k) * P.valuation (algebraMap K F k⁻¹) = 1 := by
    rw [← Valuation.map_mul, ← map_mul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hk, map_one, Valuation.map_one]

        h3.symm
    _ ≤ P.valuation (algebraMap K F k) * 1 := mul_le_mul_right h2 _
    _ = P.valuation (algebraMap K F k) := mul_one _

variable {K F} in
/-- A uniformizer at a place of `F / K` is nonzero. -/
@[category API, AMS 11 14]
theorem IsUniformizer.ne_zero {P : ValuationSubring F} (hP : IsPlace K F P) {t : F}
    (ht : IsUniformizer P t) : t ≠ 0 := by
  rintro rfl
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ : ∃ y : F, y ∉ P := by
    by_contra! h
    exact hP.2 (le_antisymm le_top fun y _ => h y)
  have hy0 : y ≠ 0 := fun h0 => hy (h0 ▸ zero_mem P)
  have hy' : P.valuation y⁻¹ < 1 := by
    rw [Valuation.map_inv, inv_lt_one₀ (zero_lt_iff.mpr ((Valuation.ne_zero_iff _).mpr hy0))]
    exact lt_of_not_ge (mt (P.valuation_le_one_iff y).mp hy)
  have := ht.2 y⁻¹ hy'
  rw [Valuation.map_zero, le_zero_iff, Valuation.zero_iff, inv_eq_zero] at this
  exact hy0 this

/-- A Kähler differential `ω ∈ Ω_{F/K}` is regular at the valuation subring `P` if
`ω = f • dt` with `f ∈ P`, for every uniformizer `t` at `P`; that is, `v_P(ω) ≥ 0`. -/
def IsRegularAt (P : ValuationSubring F) (ω : Ω[F⁄K]) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : F, IsUniformizer P t →
    ∃ f : F, P.valuation f ≤ 1 ∧ ω = f • KaehlerDifferential.D K F t

/-- The `K`-vector space of Kähler differentials of `F / K` that are regular at every place of
`F / K`, i.e. the global sections `H^0(C, Ω^1_{C/K})` of the sheaf of differentials on the
corresponding curve `C`. -/
def regularDifferentials : Submodule K Ω[F⁄K] where
  carrier := {ω | ∀ P : ValuationSubring F, IsPlace K F P → IsRegularAt K P ω}
  zero_mem' P _ t _ := ⟨0, by simp, by simp⟩
  add_mem' {ω₁ ω₂} h₁ h₂ P hP t ht := by
    obtain ⟨f₁, hf₁, rfl⟩ := h₁ P hP t ht
    obtain ⟨f₂, hf₂, rfl⟩ := h₂ P hP t ht
    exact ⟨f₁ + f₂, P.valuation.map_add_le hf₁ hf₂, (add_smul f₁ f₂ _).symm⟩
  smul_mem' k {ω} h P hP t ht := by
    obtain ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩ := h P hP t ht
    refine ⟨algebraMap K F k * f, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [Valuation.map_mul]
      exact mul_le_one' ((P.valuation_le_one_iff _).mpr (hP.1 k)) hf
    · rw [← smul_smul, algebraMap_smul]

/-- The genus of `F / K`: the dimension over `K` of the space of everywhere regular
differentials. When `F` is the function field of a smooth projective geometrically irreducible
curve `C` over `K`, this is the genus of `C`. -/

Do algebraic curves of genus $g \geq 2$ over number fields $K$ have at most some bounded number
$N(K, g)$ of $K$-rational points? That is, for every number field $K$ and every integer

    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [NumberField K] (g : ℕ), 2 ≤ g →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (F : Type v) [Field F] [Algebra K F],

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points

The conjecture asserts that for every number field $K$ and every integer $g \geq 2$ there is a
number $N(K, g)$, depending only on $K$ and $g$, such that every smooth projective geometrically
irreducible curve $C$ of genus $g$ defined over $K$ has at most $N(K, g)$ $K$-rational points.
This refines Faltings' theorem, which says that each such set $C(K)$ is finite.

Mathlib has no notion of the genus of a curve. We therefore represent a curve concretely as a
closed subscheme $V(I) \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n_K$ cut out by a homogeneous ideal $I$ of
$K[x_0, \dots, x_n]$, and we express the hypotheses "smooth, projective, geometrically
irreducible curve of genus $g$" through classical commutative algebra:
* $I \cdot \bar K[x_0, \dots, x_n]$ is a prime ideal (so $V(I)_{\bar K}$ is integral);
* the Hilbert function $t \mapsto \dim_K (K[x_0, \dots, x_n]/I)_t$ is eventually
  $d \cdot t + 1 - g$ for some $d \geq 1$ (so $V(I)$ has dimension $1$, degree $d$ and arithmetic
  genus $g$, which is the genus for a smooth geometrically integral curve);
* the Jacobian criterion: at every $\bar K$-point of $V(I)$ the gradients of the elements of $I$
  span a space of dimension $n - 1$ (so $V(I)_{\bar K}$ is nonsingular, i.e. $V(I)$ is smooth
  over $K$).

Every smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over $K$ is isomorphic to such a $V(I)$,
and the number of $K$-rational points is invariant under isomorphism, so this loses no
generality.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_rational_points)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [CHM97] Caporaso, L., Harris, J., Mazur, B., *Uniformity of rational points*,
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1997), 1–35.
* [DGH21] Dimitrov, V., Gao, Z., Habegger, P., *Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves*,
  Ann. of Math. 194 (2021), 237–298. [arXiv:2001.10276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10276)
-/

open MvPolynomial Filter
open scoped LinearAlgebra.Projectivization

namespace UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints

attribute [local instance] MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}

/-- The set of $K$-rational points of the closed subscheme $V(I) \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n_K$ cut
out by a homogeneous ideal $I \subseteq K[x_0, \dots, x_n]$: the points
$[a_0 : \dots : a_n] \in \mathbb{P}^n(K)$ at which every element of $I$ vanishes. (For a
homogeneous ideal this condition does not depend on the chosen representative of the point.) -/
def rationalPoints (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K)) : Set (ℙ K (Fin (n + 1) → K)) :=
  {P | ∀ f ∈ I, eval P.rep f = 0}

/-- The Hilbert function of the homogeneous coordinate ring $K[x_0, \dots, x_n] / I$:
`hilbertFunction I t` is the $K$-dimension of the image of the homogeneous polynomials of
degree `t` in the quotient by `I`. -/
noncomputable def hilbertFunction (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K)) (t : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K
    ((homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (n + 1)) K t).map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K I).toLinearMap)

/-- `IsSmoothCurveOfGenus I g` says that the closed subscheme $V(I) \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n_K$
defined by the ideal $I \subseteq K[x_0, \dots, x_n]$ is a smooth, projective, geometrically
irreducible curve of genus `g` over `K`. Explicitly:
* `I` is a homogeneous ideal;
* the ideal generated by `I` in $\bar K[x_0, \dots, x_n]$ is prime, i.e. $V(I)_{\bar K}$ is
  integral (in particular `I` is saturated and $V(I)$ is geometrically irreducible);
* the Hilbert function of $K[x_0, \dots, x_n] / I$ is eventually equal to $d \cdot t + 1 - g$ for
  some $d \geq 1$, i.e. $V(I)$ is one-dimensional of degree $d$ and arithmetic genus $g$; for a
  smooth geometrically integral curve the arithmetic genus is the genus;
* the Jacobian criterion holds: at every point $v \in V(I)(\bar K)$, the gradients
  $(\partial f / \partial x_j (v))_j$ of the elements $f \in I$ span a $\bar K$-vector space of
  dimension $n - 1$, i.e. $V(I)_{\bar K}$ is nonsingular at every closed point, which means that
  $V(I)$ is smooth over `K`. -/
structure IsSmoothCurveOfGenus (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K)) (g : ℕ) : Prop where
  isHomogeneous : I.IsHomogeneous (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (n + 1)) K)
  isPrime_map :
    (I.map (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))).IsPrime
  hilbertFunction_eventually_eq :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ ∀ᶠ t in atTop, (hilbertFunction I t : ℤ) = d * t + 1 - g
  finrank_span_gradient :
    ∀ v : Fin (n + 1) → AlgebraicClosure K, v ≠ 0 → (∀ f ∈ I, aeval v f = 0) →
      Module.finrank (AlgebraicClosure K) (Submodule.span (AlgebraicClosure K)
        {w | ∃ f ∈ I, w = fun j => aeval v (pderiv j f)}) + 1 = n

/-- The projective line $\mathbb{P}^1_K = V(0) \subseteq \mathbb{P}^1_K$ is a smooth curve of
genus $0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isSmoothCurveOfGenus_bot :
    IsSmoothCurveOfGenus (⊥ : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K)) 0 := by
  sorry

/-- The Fermat quartic $x_0^4 + x_1^4 + x_2^4 = 0$ in $\mathbb{P}^2_K$ is, in characteristic
zero, a smooth plane curve of degree $4$ and hence of genus $3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isSmoothCurveOfGenus_fermatQuartic [CharZero K] :
    IsSmoothCurveOfGenus
      (Ideal.span {(X 0 ^ 4 + X 1 ^ 4 + X 2 ^ 4 : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) K)}) 3 := by
  sorry

/-- **Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points.** Do algebraic curves of genus
$g \geq 2$ over number fields $K$ have at most some bounded number $N(K, g)$ of $K$-rational
points? That is: for every number field $K$ and every integer $g \geq 2$, is there a number
$N(K, g)$, depending only on $K$ and $g$, such that every smooth projective geometrically
irreducible curve $C$ of genus $g$ defined over $K$ satisfies $\#C(K) \leq N(K, g)$?

Here a curve of genus $g$ over $K$ is represented by a homogeneous ideal $I$ of
$K[x_0, \dots, x_n]$ (for some $n$) with `IsSmoothCurveOfGenus I g`, and $C(K)$ is
`rationalPoints I`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_rational_points :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] (g : ℕ), 2 ≤ g →
        ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K)),
          IsSmoothCurveOfGenus I g → (rationalPoints I).encard ≤ N := by
  sorry

end UniformBoundednessConjectureForRationalPoints
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (positive answer as the Prop; N depends only on K and g; 'algebraic curve' read as smooth/projective/geometrically irreducible; Caporaso–Harris–Mazur and Mazur's conjecture B as background only) match the source and the cited literature.
modeling_decisions: 'Algebraic curve of genus g over K' is read (following the decomposition notes and the DGH intro: 'a curve is a geometrically irreducible projective variety of dimension 1') as a smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible curve of genus g.

Curves are represented as embedded curves V(I) ⊆ ℙⁿ_K given by a homogeneous ideal I of K[x₀,…,xₙ] (quantified over all n and I) rather than as abstract Mathlib schemes. This loses no generality: every smooth projective curve over K is isomorphic to such a V(I) (take the saturated homogeneous ideal of any projective embedding), and #C(K) is an isomorphism invariant.

Geometric irreducibility is encoded as primeness of I·K̄[x₀,…,xₙ] (K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K). This is 'geometrically integral' plus saturation of I; both are harmless: smooth ⇒ reduced, so smooth + geometrically irreducible = geometrically integral, and the saturated ideal of a geometrically integral projective scheme extends to a prime ideal over K̄.

Genus is encoded via the Hilbert function of K[x]/I: eventually equal to d·t + 1 − g with d ≥ 1. For a closed subscheme X ⊆ ℙⁿ the Hilbert polynomial is χ(O_X(t)); linearity with d ≥ 1 forces dim X = 1 and non-emptiness, and P(0) = χ(O_X) = 1 − g since h⁰(O_X) = 1 for geometrically integral X and h¹(O_X) is the genus of a smooth geometrically integral curve (arithmetic genus = geometric genus).

Smoothness is encoded by the Jacobian criterion over K̄ (Hartshorne, Ex. I.5.8): at every nonzero v ∈ K̄ⁿ⁺¹ on which all f ∈ I vanish, the K̄-span of the gradients (∂f/∂xⱼ(v))ⱼ, f ∈ I, has dimension n − 1 (written `finrank + 1 = n` to avoid ℕ-truncation). Using all elements of I over K rather than generators of I·K̄[x] gives the same span at a zero (Leibniz rule). Smooth over K ⇔ X_K̄ regular at all closed points since K is perfect; the prime ideal I·K̄[x] is the full ideal of the variety X_K̄ by the Nullstellensatz, as required by the criterion.
K-rational points are `{P : ℙ K (Fin (n+1) → K) | ∀ f ∈ I, eval P.rep f = 0}`; for a homogeneous ideal this is independent of the representative and coincides with Hom_K(Spec K, V(I)).
The bound is stated as `Set.encard ≤ (N : ℕ)` (in ℕ∞), so it includes finiteness of C(K) rather than relying on Faltings' theorem; `N : ℕ` is explicitly typed so N = ⊤ is impossible.
Since the source poses a yes/no question, the statement uses `answer(sorry) ↔ …` with all quantifiers (including the number field K) inside the right-hand side, so the answer is a single truth value.

Two sorry'd `category test` declarations sanity-check the bespoke predicate on ℙ¹ (I = ⊥ in K[x₀,x₁], genus 0) and the Fermat quartic in ℙ² over a characteristic-zero field (genus 3); they are not part of the conjecture.

modeling_decisions: The yes/no question was interpreted as asking for its positive answer, with quantifier order `∀ K, ∀ g ≥ 2, ∃ N, ∀ C, #C(K) ≤ N`, so the bound depends only on K and g.

Following the decomposition notes and the cited literature, “algebraic curve” was interpreted as a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over K, rather than an arbitrary one-dimensional scheme.
The cardinality to be bounded would be the type/set of K-rational sections of the curve's structure morphism to `Spec K`; this part is expressible with existing scheme primitives.
No declaration was emitted because replacing genuine curve genus by user-supplied metadata would subtly but materially change the conjecture.

uniform_boundedness_conjecture_for_ratio.why: A faithful statement requires quantifying over smooth projective geometrically irreducible curves of a specified genus. Mathlib provides schemes, smooth/proper morphisms, pullbacks, and enough category structure to represent K-rational points as sections, but neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib provides the genus of a general algebraic curve. The available scheme-module API does not include the scheme-theoretic sheaf of Kähler differentials or coherent-sheaf cohomology needed to define genus faithfully. Packaged notions of projective morphism and geometric irreducibility are also absent (although bespoke encodings of those would be possible). Adding an arbitrary `genus : ℕ` field to curve data would not be faithful because it would allow schemes with incorrectly assigned genus. Thus the required genus-g restriction cannot currently be stated without developing substantial missing algebraic-geometry primitives.
